claims.claim_ar: الفعل «انفروا» يوجز معنى الخروج والمفارقة إلى الجهاد في كلمة واحدة، حاثًّا موجزًا ومكثَّفًا للمقصد السلوكي (الخروج للغزو).
claims.claim_en: The verb 'انفروا' condenses the meaning of leaving and going out to fight into a single, concise command — a compressed, forceful exhortation to mobilize for battle.
claims.needs_review_reason: The source chunk (Tabari) discusses the root and usages of 'نفر' and contains the substring 'انفروا', but the tafsir excerpts do not quote the exact vocalized form 'تَنْفِرُوا' from the ayah; the classification as ijaaz (conciseness) is interpretive and should be cross-checked with classical rhetorical commentary (e.g., al-Jurjani) for stronger support.

claims.source_quote_ar: ومن النفر إلى الغزو: "نَفَر فلان إلى ثغر كذا ينْفِر نَفْرًا ونَفِيرًا"
claims.claim_ar: تكرار صيغ الجذر «ن-ف-ر» (نَفَر، نَفِير، نَفْرًا) في الخطاب والتعليق يخلق إيقاعًا وتأكيدًا دلاليًّا على فعل الخروج والفرقة، فيؤكّد موضوع الحثّ على النفير.
claims.claim_en: The repeated morphological forms of the root n-f-r (nafar, nafeer, nafran) in the discourse create rhythm and semantic emphasis on the act of departing, reinforcing the exhortation to mobilize.
claims.needs_review_reason: The quoted tafsir passage (Tabari) explicitly lists multiple forms of the root, supporting a claim of morphological repetition; labeling this as the badi device 'takrar' (repetition) is plausible but should be checked against purer badi classifications in the classical sources requested (al-Jurjani, al-Sakkaki, etc.).
